order: Roster order on the italy sheet puts liguria-valle-d-aosta before calabria-basilicata, so the file holds them in that order.
check: check-fragment reports one problem per article and nothing else: regions[i].deeper is required for an article off the map. This edition writes no deeper list (the task's rule, as in c1 and c2), so the integrator relaxes that .more rule; with only that rule relaxed the file passes whole, with no superlative note. Not deepened, each article is held to the one prose total (800 to 1,800 words, every place note counted), 6 to 14 cards and 6 to 12 questions with at least 3 multiple choice. No key is the longest option.
cms: central-southern-italy (the Court's pages 34 and 35) names Basilicata and Calabria as regions to place on a map, the Mediterranean climate of the south, the Apennines, the Ligurian, Tyrrhenian and Adriatic seas, Aglianico, IGP, DOC and DOCG, Superiore and Riserva, and producers; every row that touches these places is covered (both regions placed between their seas, the Mediterranean coasts against the cooler Vulture, Aglianico, the three tiers, Superiore and Riserva as Aglianico del Vulture defines them, a decanting line for young Aglianico del Vulture). The Ligurian Sea rows of central-southern-italy and tuscany are covered in Liguria's water and topography. No CMS subject writes a row for Liguria's wines or for the Valle d'Aosta; the Codex's own Village bank (Pigato as Vermentino, Sciacchetrà, Prié Blanc, Picotendro, Petite Arvine, Gaglioppo at Cirò, Superiore for the Vulture DOCG, Greco di Bianco) is covered untagged, its Grand Cru items (Donnas and Carema's stone pillared pergolas, Cirò's Krimisa claim) are tagged master.
aliases: Every roster alias is claimed. Added for Liguria and Valle d'Aosta: cinque terre sciacchetra, riviera di ponente, riviera di levante, dolceacqua, ormeasco di pornassio, pornassio, golfo del tigullio portofino, colline di levanto, val polcevera, aosta valley, morgex, chambave, arnad montjovet. Added for Calabria and Basilicata: ciro classico, ciro marina, lamezia, terre di cosenza, bivongi, scavigna, lucania, aglianico del vulture superiore, venosa, terre dell alta val d agri, grottino di roccanova. Not claimed, because italy.3.json sends them to campania and they are not roster aliases that apply-roster moves: barile, monte vulture, rionero in vulture; the integrator may move them to calabria-basilicata with the roster's basilicata, vulture, aglianico del vulture, calabria and ciro. Campania's place 'Basilicata, the neighbour to the east' becomes the roster's one line pointer (takes).

articles.name: Liguria and Valle d'Aosta
uncertain: Liguria's DOC count differs by source (eight, nine or eleven, depending on whether Sciacchetrà and sub-zones count apart), so no count is given; that Liguria has no DOCG is agreed.

Rossese di Dolceacqua as the first Ligurian DOC in 1972 rests on a 2022 press piece marking fifty years and the reference summaries; Cinque Terre's 29 May 1973 on lecinqueterre.org and the Cinque Terre DOC summaries. Neither disciplinare was read; the integrator or refuter may wish to cite them.
Ormeasco di Pornassio as a DOC of its own from 2003 rests on two secondary summaries.

Sciacchetrà's grape shares conflict (Bosco at least 40 per cent in some sources, at least 60 per cent on the park site), so no figure is given; a November pressing date and a Riserva of three years each rest on one source and are left out.

The Valle d'Aosta DOC's date conflicts (1971, 1985 and 1986 in different sources), so it is left undated; that it absorbed the older Donnas and Enfer d'Arvier DOCs is agreed. Torrette's 70 per cent Petit Rouge and Donnas's 85 per cent Nebbiolo rest on one secondary source each and are left out. No amendment from 2020 to 2026 was found in one search.
Blanc de Morgex et de La Salle at about 900 to 1,200 metres, ungrafted on low pergolas, rests on the Chambre valdôtaine and the regional tourism site, and agrees with the Codex's Village bank.
The Valle d'Aosta as Italy's smallest wine region is a measured superlative the Codex's Régionale bank asks; it is kept, resting on the reference works.
Albarola and Bianchetta Genovese are kept as two names; an identity between them was not checked and is not claimed.
Producers whose trading name is a living person's full name are left out (several Ligurian and Valdostan estates).

articles.name: Calabria and Basilicata
uncertain: The law change of the chunk: Cirò Classico was registered as a DOCG by the European Union in 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/1518, July 2025, by the reports), Calabria's first: red only, at least 90 per cent Gaglioppo with up to 10 per cent Magliocco or Greco Nero, from the communes of Cirò and Cirò Marina, at least three years of ageing with six months in wood (Decanter and Gambero Rosso agree). The regulation itself was not read; the regulation number and the 13 per cent alcohol one source gives are left out. Whether the DOC's own Rosso Classico name survives beside the DOCG is not claimed (the wine is written Cirò Rosso and Cirò Classico).

Cirò DOC dated 1969 (the AIS copy of the disciplinare and Decanter; one source says 1959); its 80 per cent Gaglioppo for red and rosé and 80 per cent Greco Bianco for white rest on the same two. Higher shares in other sources describe the older rule or habit.

Aglianico del Vulture DOC 18 February 1971 and the Superiore DOCG of 2 August 2010 (last modified 3 July 2014) rest on the disciplinari and Italian Wine Central; the Superiore's three years with twelve months in wood and twelve in bottle, five years for the Riserva and 13.5 per cent alcohol on the disciplinare and Italian Wine Central. The Riserva's 24 months in wood (one source) is left out. Wholly Aglianico rests on Italian Wine Central and the reference works. No amendment after 2014 was found.

Greco di Bianco's date (1980) and its 95 per cent Greco Bianco rest on one secondary source and are left out. The identity of the Greco Bianco of Bianco with Malvasia di Lipari is disputed between sources and is not claimed; the article says only that it is a different vine from Campania's Greco.
Gaglioppo's parentage (Mantonico Bianco as one parent is reported; Sangiovese as the other was not confirmed) is left out.

Basilicata's other DOCs are named without dates (Matera, Terre dell'Alta Val d'Agri, Grottino di Roccanova); Matera's red blend called Moro and its grape shares were not checked and are written only as red blends.
Cirò's descent from Krimisa, a wine said to have been given to Olympic victors, is written as a claim and a legend, as the Codex's Grand Cru bank asks it.

Paternoster carries its WINE_PRODUCERS id and founding year (1925) from the Codex's own producer file. Elena Fucci (p-elena-fucci) is left out because its trading name is a living person's full name; the same doubt leaves out other estates named for living people.
